Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

schema.description: The VTC tells a member that a step-up passkey was enrolled for them or revoked from them, naming who acted and when. Unsolicited: the member did not ask, and may be offline.

by.description: Who acted: the member themselves (equal to `did`) when they enrolled or revoked it on their own session, or an administrator's DID when they invited the enrollment or revoked for the member. A `by` other than `did` is the signal this task exists to carry — act on someone else's behalf is exactly the account-takeover shape a silent change would hide.

credentialId.description: Durable identifier of the step-up credential, as auth/passkey/revoke/start and auth/passkey/admin-list carry it: opaque, non-secret metadata, never key material. Lets the member recognise or distinguish a credential without disclosing anything that would help an attacker.

did.description: The member's own DID — the notice's recipient. Carried in the payload as well as the envelope so that a forwarded notice, detached from its transport, still names its subject.

event.description: `enrolled` — a step-up passkey (auth/passkey/enroll/invite or auth/passkey/enroll/finish, purpose stepUp) is now bound to the member. `revoked` — one was unbound (auth/passkey/revoke/finish).

occurredAt.description: When the event took effect at the VTC — not when the notice was sent, which differs whenever the member was offline.

reason.description: The acting administrator's stated reason, verbatim, when one was given. Absent rather than empty when none was: a community that chose not to explain is itself information. Never populated for a member acting on their own credential — they already know why.

schema.title: VTC Members — Step-up Passkey Notice — payload
